# PR21: UI and log leftovers

Implementation and review snapshot for PR #158. All four PR21 items were rechecked against the merged PR20 code. They remain applicable, with the history fixes now owned by the server projection and paginated history hook rather than the plan's older URL helper reference.

## Changes and impact

- AI history combines attributed normal rows with surviving AI-only records. It deduplicates mirrors before filtering, pagination, totals, and exports; anonymous repeated appends remain separate. AI rows sort by timestamp with a stable logical-entry tie-breaker; normal and system views keep file order. Shared classification and model-identity helpers run at ingestion and in the client. Stored projection fields avoid JSON parsing for AI/model filters and line counts. Log writes and stored channel formats are unchanged; the disposable projection schema changes. Missing audience/kind fields use the same inference before indexing and raw-file reads, so plain model output remains in ALL totals, pages, and exports. Sparse session rows retain the live client's session kind, protecting activity detection after reload. Explicit fields and SYS milestone classification are preserved.
- Newest history responses include sorted `modelIds` across the ticket, phase, attempt, and bead scope, independent of the selected view/model and page limit. Older pages and export walks omit the additional aggregate. Phase logs and Full Log share this catalog in React Query across filter loading and component remounts; cached pages cannot replay older metadata. Scope changes reset selection to ALL. Pending/error selection, display, metrics, and export remain aligned, including unavailable initial models and live-only tabs. Initial loading and known-empty views without live rows disable copy; empty export responses leave the clipboard unchanged and report no new outcome; target changes cancel pending exports. No additional endpoint or request is needed.
- The model picker uses a search combobox and grouped options-only listbox. Provider-collapse controls move above the results. Tab moves among search and controls rather than each model row. Arrow keys navigate options and Enter accepts; Home/End retain native text editing. Contextual labels identify the main/council picker and current choice; encoded IDs, unobscured active options, announced empty-search results, and a collapsed-results message complete the behavior. Filtering, disabled choices, mouse selection, Escape, and focus restoration remain available.
- Execution-setup step controls expose expanded state and controlled-panel IDs. Clipboard callers, including crash details, show `Copy failed` until a retry succeeds or the logical target changes; each failed retry remounts its alert. Status changes within the same log-row identity preserve feedback. Retry icons remain visible on failure or keyboard focus, and truncated-log feedback stays with sticky actions. Phase/full-log export failure clears any previous success indicator, and obsolete exports are cancelled.

The owner approved complete model metadata, moving provider-collapse controls above results, and the wording `Copy failed`. The owner also approved target-change copy resets, repeated announcements, and timestamp-ordered AI-only recovery. All follow-up work stays on the same branch and PR, unmerged. Every local and bot review finding has a disposition in [the review record](pr21-review-dispositions.md).

## Documentation and verification

The changelog records all four changes. Website `docs/frontend.md` and `docs/api-reference.md` describe them as unreleased; no CLI reference or release pin changes. No workflow status definitions, prompts, parsers, dependencies, or ignore rules need changes.

Regression tests cover restored milestones, paging/export filters, complete model discovery, stale tabs and cached catalogs, scope changes, combobox navigation, disclosures, and clipboard refusal/retry. Local Chromium checks use the real components with isolated fixture responses; they do not start a ticket lifecycle. Full lint, typechecking, unit/integration tests, application build, and package checks run locally. CI completion and PR reviews remain with the owner.

Accessibility follows the [W3C combobox pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/). Conditional render-time state adjustment follows [React's guidance](https://react.dev/learn/you-might-not-need-an-effect#adjusting-some-state-when-a-prop-changes) so an invalid tab's old query is corrected before the fallback view is committed.
